reviews.text: The Flash (2023) is hopelessly lost in its multiversal lore, amounting to nothing more than action figures brawling while actual characters or emotions get left in the dust.
reviews.author: Justin Kim

reviews.text: The film’s convoluted parallel plot adds almost nothing to the impact of the storytelling, other than to make it feel muddled.
reviews.author: Christina Newland

reviews.text: For a film about a very fast man, the narrative is slow at times. The tacky CGI and video game artistry make the experience less immersive too.
reviews.author: Udita Jhunjhunwala

reviews.text: Michael Keaton is the main reason to see “The Flash” (2023), the 13th film in the DC Extended Universe.  Feel free to arrive at the theater under one hour late to see a decent Batman sequel otherwise you will be peeking at your watch
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: For 2/3 of The Flash -- and it's too long -- it's kind of fun... in the last sections it becomes slightly video game-ish.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Despite having fun throughout, The Flashisn't flawless, especially in its final act. But Miller as the eponymous superhero is clearly having fun, and so are the other key characters that wouldn't think twice.
reviews.author: Vinamra Mathur

reviews.text: Simply put, this movie is way fun and worth a watch in the theaters, put it on your list of to-do's this weekend.
reviews.author: Derek Sante

reviews.text: Given that seemingly every piece of media is unleashing its perception of whatever the multiverse may be, it’s refreshing that The Flash treats it as more of an existential test.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: ... fun, generous, and entertaining. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Andrea Zamora

reviews.text: The Flash may be the most underrated, most underappreciated movie of the year.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Are multiverses just an excuse for not picking a tone or choosing a story? Our cinema’s flavor of the last few years may just be the child of channel-surfing... The Flash makes you feel simultaneously overserved and underserved.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: The Flash creates not just an origin story but lays the foundation for an emotional and layered performance few expect from superhero movies. He can see how things could have been, allowing him to question how he became the man and hero he believes he is.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: The result of literally decades of unsuccessful development, culminating in something that – if not borderline unwatchable – is certainly the most pronounced death throe of Warner Bros’ DC Extended Universe to date.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: Color me shocked.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Overall, The Flash is one of the better DCEU entries, but that’s not saying much for a universe of films often found thin or clunky. Muschietti focuses on the human side of meta-human Barry and that leads to a solid emotional journey.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Peterson

reviews.text: Perhaps the main problem with The Flash is there is too much of everything packed into its not short runtime. By the time we get to the final crisis of universes colliding it seems so inevitable that it’s tiring.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: With eighty percent of The Flash devoted to other DC heroes and underwhelming visual effects, the result seems like a foregone conclusion.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: The Flash has about two-thirds of a decent storyline, utilizing a much better characterization of the beloved superhero than we saw previously in the DC cinematic universe, but sadly the film is let down by a final act that unravels into a muddled mess.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: Ezra Miller’s superhero outing has an affecting storyline, fan service aplenty, and an easy-way-out anticlimax; maybe this is a befitting conclusion to the DCEU storyline.
reviews.author: Bhuvanesh Chandar

reviews.text: Ultimately, what you want to know, dear reader, is whether or not the film is worth your time? The best answer I can offer is: sorta.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: The characters are so driven that the film’s most earth-shattering moments don’t come during an epic battle, but in quiet moments of reflection and recognition of one’s responsibility. If you can get beyond multiverse overkill, this one is worth watching.
reviews.author: Lee Zumpe

reviews.text: It's an irregular superhero film that, with a handful of cameos and visual pyrotechnics, gets off to a fast-paced start by showing the origin of a solid Barry Allen played by Miller, but whose flashes fade at considerable speed. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Setting aside the actor’s numerous legal issues, Miller turns in a masterful pair of performances.
reviews.author: Kevin Slane

reviews.text: Director Andy Muschietti does little to make the front half of the film interesting other than to try to explain the always complicated rules of time travel.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: The thing that sticks with you about The Flash is that crazy baby shower.
reviews.author: Tim Miller

reviews.text: The Flash is a highly entertaining film that strikes a balance between emotional depth and nostalgia. While there are moments of uneven CGI and pacing, the movie shines as one of the most well-written and genuinely satisfying DCEU entries in a long time.
reviews.author: Surya Komal

reviews.text: The interesting, profound parallels between Barry Allen's arcs, the emotional moral dilemmas about life's scars, and the return of Danny Elfman's iconic Batman theme are some of the aspects that make this blockbuster a very satisfying, nostalgic viewing.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: The issues in "The Flash" come down to the fact that anyone under a certain age might not understand or care about all of the '90s sentimentality at the center of the story. Surprises abound, some in poor taste.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: Fortunately, "The Flash" comes with enough twists and tricks to keep things from being stale. And a large part of that is seeing Michael Keaton suit up as Batman again for the first time in more than 30 years.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: The fact that The Flash exists as a film is itself something of a miracle (albeit one driven purely by economics), but the fact that it's also actually really damn good...Well, just who on earth saw that coming?
reviews.author: Ilan Preskovsky

reviews.text: Feeling like disparate pieces that don't stitch together to make the best whole isn't what The Flash was aiming for, but it's what's been zapped into cinemas.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: The Flash isn’t exactly a bad film but many fans will expect a lot more from it. There is enough in the film to suggest that the next films in the DC universe could be something special.
reviews.author: David Griffiths

reviews.text: It’s extremely entertaining, surprisingly funny but more importantly, it has a great emotional story with a lot of heart. Now I’m not crowning it the greatest CBM ever but it’s definitely a MUST SEE!
reviews.author: Elliott Collins

reviews.text: For a film that references Back to the Future throughout, it sure didn't follow the same formula, but it's still fun enough to see in theatres.
reviews.author: Lauren Veneziani

reviews.text:
Defying all odds THE FLASH is incredible. Purely special in so many ways. 
Incredible performances, incredible action scenes, an incredibly emotional tale that at the center of its story is Barry Allen. This is a what if Tim Burton Directed A Flash film
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: "The Flash” offers some general interest to fans of the swift, fleet-of-foot character, but ultimately, the movie is a meandering, multi-layered CGI-laden drama that offers little that’s new.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: A buddy movie packed with action and time-traveling that turns out to be much more insightful and exhilarating than one could have expected. Unfortunately, the duality of the two Barry Allen protagonists ends up becoming a metaphor for its inconsistency.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: The Flash may be fast, but he’s still a step behind the cinematic competition. There’s some diverting entertainment to be had here, but just as many opportunities to be baffled or annoyed.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Going back in time and revisiting nearly every previous era of DC in order to tell a story about the importance of letting go, The Flash is just running in place.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: The Flash isn't totally devoid of pathos, and Keaton provides a ton of nostalgia-heavy fun. But its odd aesthetic choices and circular storytelling resulted in a final product that's more of an exhausting marathon than breezy jog.
reviews.author: Joshua Axelrod

reviews.text: Keaton's easily the best part of a flawed movie, one that leans hard on viewer nostalgia instead of a screenplay that holds together.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Michael Keaton does stand out as an aging Batman, called to fight yet another time. Keaton’s eyebrows were always expressive.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: The Flash is not without flaws – but those are inherent in many films within the genre, like the over-stuffed CG filled finale. However, for the most part The Flash is an excellent superhero adventure that has plenty to offer its audience.
reviews.author: Niall Browne

reviews.text: A watered down slap stick version The Flashpoint Paradox storyline.
reviews.author: Alachia Queen

reviews.text: After the dimension-hopping possibilities explored in “Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse,” the options of the multiverse shown here — even in the grand finale, which resurrects three deceased actors through CGI — feel pedestrian.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: When the film comes to its point, it tries too hard to impress its multi-verse view. What we leave with is this: If producers don’t like an actor in a role, they’ve got the ability to recast. No one, apparently, is safe.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: Ezra Miller’s performance is fantastic, and I also enjoyed seeing Michael Keaton’s performance as Batman; there are surprise cameos by other Marvel superheroes as well.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: Sadly, the studio did this movie no favors by releasing it hot on the heels of the excellent Spider-Man: Across The Spider-Verse, which follows similar themes in a superior superhero saga. The Flash may be fast, but it feels late to the party.
reviews.author: Erin Maxwell

reviews.text: “The Flash” is centered in the sweet spot between action, comedy, and heart because is is grounded in a deep affection for the source material but is not afraid to play with some of its absurdities.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: My inner comic book geek beamed, while still mindful of the film's place in the bigger picture, both for the future of its lead actor's career and the future of movies based on DC Comics.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: 2023 was the year the superhero bubble finally burst. Warner Bros. scrapped Batgirl to bet the farm on walking PR disaster Ezra Miller. They lost $200 million on what is easily the worst film of the decade so far.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: The Flash feels like a comic book come alive.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: It is a complicated story, but it makes sense within its own space. I hope that Ezra Miller continues to play The Flash. He is a fine actor. If you don't think so, just check out his performance in 'The Perks of Being a Wallflower' sometime.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Blame the ancient Greeks for inventing the general idea of the multiverse. Blame DC for propagating the concept in one of its Flash comics in 1961. And blame anyone you like for this hot mess of a film.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: It's funny here and there... But overall, it's kind of a mess.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Forever threatening to consume itself literally as well as philosophically, The Flash is redeemed by its edgy humour, Ezra Miller’s investment, and Muschietti’s adept staging of the numerous action scenes.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: Warner’s $220 million, CGI-filled bomb is what happens when superhero movies peddle in nostalgia for a history that doesn’t exist.
reviews.author: Charles Holmes

reviews.text: The whole experience perpetually comes across like a first draft that nobody cared to revise, exuding the same sloppy mediocrity that’s defined the canon-level disgrace known as the DCEU.
reviews.author: Ian Thomas Malone

reviews.text: The moments of blatant fan service will undoubtedly make nerds happy, but the story doesn’t stand up to scrutiny, and frankly, that fan service is an empty gesture because the multiverse presented here is totally unimaginative.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: The Flash is not the worst of its kind, although it definitely is one of the most vacuous expeditions into the multiverse.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: Keaton's appearance is also nostalgic, of course, and there are a host of Easter eggs and cameos that will make audiences either applaud, laugh, or roll their eyes, depending on how they feel about the sentimentality of the sequence.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: This movie is absolutely insane. It has horrible CGI at times but huge creativity at others. The cast works really well and the storyline actually works well in the multiverse. I enjoyed this hot mess way more than I thought I would.
reviews.author: Adam Olinger

reviews.text: The Flash is far from being that disastrous movie most seem to derive solely based on box office numbers. As a Superhero Movie is for sure within standard, nitpicking aside. Genre fatigue + multiverse movies saturation might be the actual cultprits here.
reviews.author: Alejandro Turdó

reviews.text: And it has a heart—sometimes it's in tachycardia and in danger of sputtering out, but it's there.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: The Flash is the type of film that is at best a grave example of “superhero fatigue” and at worst, a harsh reminder of the greatness we could have received.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: The first superhero with chest hair. Miller is terrific. The film is fun and good. What happened to Christian Bale, Val Kilmer and shamefully, why ignore the 21ST Century’s Superman, Henry Cavill?
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: ...increasingly underwhelming...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Andy Muschietti's jittery, frenetic The Flash has about it the feeling of someone getting away with something.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: This overstuffed helping of DC Comics chaos has trouble sustaining engagement beyond maybe the first hour and a half of its two-hour and 24-minute run time.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Steady action pairs exceedingly well with the humor and world-building of Hodson's script.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: In drama & in life, “anything is possible” does the opposite of making things compelling and beautiful; it makes things boring. As Michael Keaton’s Bruce Wayne describes it in The Flash (with an amusing spaghetti metaphor), the multiverse is a “hot mess.”
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: This DC movie felt like a franchise upgrade. The story was interesting and didn’t feel like DC was trying too hard to be like Marvel (although the multi-verse timing is a bit too close to its rival). For once, DC has a story that could just be DC.
reviews.author: Reginald Ponder

reviews.text: The Flash is an entertaining enough film that will please most crowds, with good performances from Miller, Keaton and Calle.
reviews.author: Ricky Church

reviews.text: The film is enormously entertaining.
reviews.author: Dave Golder

reviews.text: This is the way the DC Extended Universe ends: not with a bang, but with grating comedy, momentumless action, and convictions so flimsy that they cancel themselves out.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: The film works really well... it's powerful.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: The Flash is great fun, mostly well-made, and thoroughly enjoyable.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: The Flash is a spectacular blockbuster that wipes the slate clean for an exciting future. Not everything in the DC Universe worked, but at least it can go out with a bang.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: We've already seen this premise four or five times, but this is oddly one of the better versions of it, thanks to action scenes that feel like more than placeholders.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Neither a cinematographic nor a communal experience, The Flash is a visual list of fleeting, disposable moments... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: The special effects aren't particularly flashy, and Flash's races are singularly clumsy. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: A dull, overly-saturated CGI action movie mess, that’s both half an hour too long (as per usual!) and rushed.
reviews.author: Erik Kain

reviews.text: There was some optimism that this film could stick the landing and pass the torch to James Gun and company. Sadly though, that wasn’t really the case.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: As a Justice League member, the Flash, as portrayed by Ezra Miller, was an entertaining character who excelled in scene-stealing moments and provided comic relief. However, as the main character his obnoxiousness is overwhelming.
reviews.author: Dustin Rowles

reviews.text: The Flash is far from perfect but it will do while we wait for Indiana Jones’s return.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: The Flash strikes an impressive balance of the zany Allen antics the character is known for with the crushing inevitability of the plot.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: When The Flash isn’t consumed by lengthy aerial battles and whirling roundabouts of effects, tossing out names and faces of nearly everyone who has worn a hero cape, the movie’s hero embarks on a real journey, falling short in the final steps.
reviews.author: Justine Elias

reviews.text: While everything swells to the expected hyper-cartoonish climax, director Andy Muschietti and writer Christina Hodson impressively keep the story centred on the people, leaving the apocalyptic elements as merely plot points, as they should be.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Its action, while ugly, is appropriately kinetic and fabulously inventive.
reviews.author: Joel Harley

reviews.text: ... An avalanche of wax figures that captures the worst of cameo culture, digital necrophilia and nostalgia manipulation. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: At its best it speeds along with its own style and a strong ensemble. Most importantly, it's genuinely fun.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Director Andy Muschietti and Hodson and lead actor Miller all do well with what’s most important, which is character.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: It all moves along rather zippily until director Andy Muschietti tries to restage the 2013 film's CGI-heavy finale.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: A humorous and heartfelt examination of loss and acceptance with strong lead performances and fun action — a celebration of DC’s cinematic history.
reviews.author: Jonathan Garcia

reviews.text: The Flash is really well constructed, including giving viewers the character’s origin without being an origin story. It's more of a lighthearted, comedy-heavy movie that still makes the emotional moments land.
reviews.author: Eric Goldman

reviews.text: The Flash is certainly fun, packed with some great action and surprising emotion, it's just erratic in its consistency…and those visuals…damn.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: It's not a total mess, but this mashup of ideas lacks tight and quality execution, resulting in a few highlights and a lot of missed opportunities that might have made this a story worth telling.
reviews.author: Patrick Hicks

reviews.text: It's freaking bananas that we get to see Michael Keaton as Batman again.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: This is the worst film I have seen in 2023. I genuinely despise it. Don’t waste your time or your money. If you’d like to see Keaton and Calle’s good work amidst the dreck, wait until it comes to the library.
reviews.author: Justin Harrison

reviews.text: When it works, the film moves like a bullet. When it stumbles? Like the greatest characters in comics, and like life, the one enemy The Flash can’t outrun is itself.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: I appreciated its self-referential style, the well-timed laughs, the good pacing, the open-armed embrace of nostalgia, and the way it left a big smile on my face.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Call me old-fashioned but I liked the steroidal-ly jacked, testosterone-fueled, early comic book superheros the way I like a '69 Camaro with a powerfully configured V-8 engine. So I'm not a fan of the new, skinny Spider-Men, nor of this new skinny Flash.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: There are authentic, interesting, and original comic book movies that deserve respect -- 'The Flash' just isn't one of them.
reviews.author: Annie Banks

reviews.text: Most disappointingly, Keaton's Batman hasn’t been written as the kinky weirdo from the Burton movies. He’s just another retro nostalgia prop in a film overwhelmed by references and inside jokes.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: It’s efficient, pacy and largely enjoyable stuff.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: 'The Flash' is bright and fleet-footed, continuing DC's welcome departure from the leaden, sluggish, grayness of the early entries.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: A thundering mess that ends with the usual boring battle in a CGI sky. But, on a scene-by-scene basis, The Flash passes the time better than Gunn’s own puzzlingly lauded Suicide Squad.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: The Flash goes down like a sparkling tonic...due to the lively, strong performance of nonbinary actor Ezra Miller, who, personal and legal issues aside, is captivating as Barry Allen, the fastest man alive.
reviews.author: Randy Shulman

reviews.text: Just know that this latest Justice League entry soars from the start with a literal "baby shower" event before ultimately slowing a bit down a lengthy final stretch that enjoys one last -- of many -- surprise cameos.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Flashy and fun whenever not adhering to nostalgia requirements and delivering uncanny PS3-era graphics, The Flash arrives as a dazzling delight.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: The low bar of expectations and shrug of a release mean that the film actually has the space to feel breezy and amusing in its very okayness.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: Ezra Miller brings surprising emotional depth to DC’s greatest-hits spectacular which will impact nostalgic fans the most. My favorite performance goes to Sasha Calle as Kara Zor-El a.k.a. Supergirl.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: It may be a round-about origin story, but it gets the job done with unusual bravado and a distinct style ... unfortunately, or fortunately, or wherever you rest on the gray matter of Miller's [abuse accusations], Miller is very good at being Barry Allen.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Beyond Keaton, there really isn't much there. Miller's dual role doesn't work, with the younger Barry growing tiresome rather quickly and the banter between the two characters more annoying than fun.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Keaton, like the character he’s playing, has had several decades to think about what being Batman might really mean -- and his prickly, complicated presence has a gravity the movie otherwise strives for but seldom achieves.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: The action scenes capture the scale of people with otherworldly powers, but it’s a cheap thrill, not genuine awe, like video game levels or, ahem, theme park rides. It’s ~150 minutes that go by quite slowly.
reviews.author: Jack Riedy

reviews.text: Despite an old-fashioned gee-whiz spirit and the incredibly welcome return of Michael Keaton as Batman, DC’s ‘The Flash’ suffers from a bad case of multiverse overkill.
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: The film’s Big Theme is a warning against too much looking back, wishing you could change things, instead of moving forward. A lesson The Flash itself doesn’t always hear, but one that could prove valuable for the upcoming DC Extended Universe reset.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: If these misbegotten DC movies can’t outrun their past, running back into it is the next best thing. And “the next best thing” pretty well sums up The Flash.
reviews.author: Chris Klimek

reviews.text: A high-water mark in the concluding DC Extended Universe, the film manages to give us plenty of spectacle as well as some decent emotional moments.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: It director Andy Muschietti’s timeline jumping journey is corporate synergy at its absolute worst.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: It’s one of the finest DC films, hitting just the right notes in every department, be it humour, drama or computer imagery.
reviews.author: Devesh Sharma

reviews.text: Unfortunately the best aspects of the film are drowned out by a sea of middle-school humor, silly plot twists and weak acting, especially by Ezra Miller in the title role.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: There are decent visuals, surreal and spectacular CGI and a couple of titter-out-loud moments. But hypocritical Hollywood seems to have forgotten all about the #MeToo movement in a flash.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: It’s impossible to take your eyes off Keaton’s Batman but, while he’s the film’s MVP, Sasha Calle’s Supergirl is close behind.
reviews.author: Freda Cooper

reviews.text: Every time I think I’ve become completely fatigued by live-action superhero movies, one comes along to restore my faith. The Flash is the latest to do that.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The Flash has its problems, but they’re outweighed just enough by the story and characters (and surprises) to make the movie work.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Andy Muschietti has no story to tell, so must be content with an overwrought comic restyling of old movie memorabilia, with the requisite corporate lacquer applied to ensure it’s as synthetic, witless, and wearying as possible.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: The movie lags only during the lengthy CGI fights when Barry I and Barry II go up against evil General Zod. But Miller is so fresh and charismatic that he doesn’t need so much special-effects padding.
reviews.author: Dana Kennedy

reviews.text: As it is, there’s the pesky way the multiverse dulls the dramatic edge of death, even as the film seeks to sharpen the blade.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: It's IP-plugging for the easy to please fandom.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: The special effects are tacky, and the film’s frequent recourse to other DC characters creates an air of desperation.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: There is a lot of good in this film. There's also quite a fair amount of bad -- and so many quips, cameos, characters, explosions, and rewinds of movies you've already seen, that you might not even care to give a yay/nay to this particular [film].
reviews.author: Brady Langmann

reviews.text: Calle really does a commendable job, and she shines on the screen alongside Miller.
reviews.author: Theolin Tembo

reviews.text: A nice surprise. It’s another multiverse story, but one that keeps the storytelling lean and not too complicated
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Stuffed with unnecessary cameos seemingly for the sake of it, "The Flash" contains glimpses of fun, but is tonally uneven. It's often in conflict with itself over whether it wants to be a Batman nostalgia fest or about the fastest man alive.
reviews.author: Kirsten Acuna

reviews.text: Usually, a critic's complaint is that these super-productions waste first-rate special effects on mediocre screenplays. In The Flash, is criminally reprehensible that it's the other way around... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: The Flash isn’t the first movie to seem like it’s been cursed, but the multitude of ways in which the production misfired is frankly bizarre and somewhat unprecedented.
reviews.author: Miles Surrey

reviews.text: As directed by Andy Muschietti from Christina Hodson's screenplay, it wastes no time in establishing a tongue-in-cheek, self-referential style, playing Barry's initial adventure of the film mostly for giddy laughs.
reviews.author: John Paul King

reviews.text: Despite the effects being very 'Polar Express', the creativity and emotional moments work well enough to make this film worth recommending.
reviews.author: Doug Walker

reviews.text: The Flash is no genre-redefining masterpiece and it’s unlikely to appeal to viewers who aren’t already bought into the superhero oeuvre, but it’s a much better movie than what’s being advertised.
reviews.author: Dylan Roth

reviews.text: Andy Muschietti manages to create one of the best films of the DC multi-universe so far, with enough action doses, a sensational plot, the charisma of new superheroes and the nostalgia of heroes of the past. {Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Laura Hiros

reviews.text: Troubled actor Ezra Miller is gifted comic talent, lots of fan service and game of: Who's your favorite Batman? Superman?
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Funny, tightly paced, and full of action like its titular hero. But it trips over itself in the final stretch, and in imparting a lesson to the protagonist but also wanting a last-minute feel-good twist, it tries to have its cake and eat it too.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: The film's strength is its invention and nostalgia, which captured this old comic book reader with emotion I wasn’t prepared to feel, and a renewal of love for what brought me into that theater seat. Great performances, surprises and other super-latives!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: The action is swift, the dialogue is funny and there’s a multiverse of surprise cameos. Ironically, “The Flash” is half-hour too long. Even so, it’s a suitably electric comic book flick.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: ... strikes a successful balance between its fan service obligations and forging a path of its own with surprising emotional depth.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Fast-paced and unabashedly fun, the speedy supe goes back in time to save his mother and makes a mess of the multiverse. Much fan-servicing, particularly with Michael Keaton's Batman reprise, but well done in one of the best DCEU films so far.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Ezra Miller is razor sharp  and Sasha Calle inhabits Supergirl with a zest and fervor letting the audience know that 'girl' may be part of her name, but she is super in every sense of the word. Despite the controversy, The Flash is great summer fun!
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: the movie has plenty of fan-pleasing moments...[but] there is nothing in “The Flash” to rival Evan Peters’ Quicksilver scene in “X-Men: Days of Future Past.”
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: I have seen anthropomorphic mucus characters in pharmaceutical commercials that look better than most of this film. The CGI is so bad, I think I hate computers now. Bring the abacus back.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Mad trippy or catastrophic? This DC superhero epic is actually a mix of both, dragged down by exhausting multiverse hopping but flashy fun on the wings of virtuoso Ezra Miller and the grumpy comic perfection of Michael Keaton as a Batman on the ropes.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: The cast makes this one of the more entertaining DC films in recent memory, elevating the material far above what’s on the page and on the storyboards. It might not strike like lightning, but it’s still a comforting breeze.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: The Flash’s above-average performances and thrilling action scenes make it a very watchable popcorn blockbuster for much of its runtime. However, excessive fan service and unconvincing CGI trip the film up long before its end credits roll.
reviews.author: Leon Miller

reviews.text: I mostly enjoyed The Flash. But the most confusing aspect of all this is the continued brand maintenance, the ongoing effort to rescue certain parts of the so-called DCEU from obsolescence even as the rest of it comes to an end.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: When the movie is fun, it’s very fun.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: The Flash Movie isn't the GREATEST superhero movie ever made, but it's a damn good one full of humor, awesome action sequences and a touching story with a little Latin flavor on top! Ezra Miller is fantastic, BUT Keaton and Sasha Calle steal this movie.
reviews.author: John Rocha

reviews.text: Barry’s inability to get through his grief ... works as a crucial plot point, an emotional pivot, and thanks, surprisingly enough to Miller’s layered performance, a reminder of what superhero storytelling can deliver beyond visual pyrotechnics.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: The Multiverse's bottomless stockpile of do-overs and variant replacement characters was already getting on my nerves in the Marvel flicks, and this DC spin on it has the same effect: a dilution of the dramatic stakes.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: Felt like a two hour comic book movie constructed by a committee. Andy Muschietti deserves so much better.
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: While it may not be a resounding triumph, it isn’t the DC dud it might have been.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: [Miller] gives Barry a real sweetness, and the performance holds the movie together.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: The Flash concludes as a mirthless parade, one of exhumations and sad nostalgia trips. For a movie about a racer hero, it’s weirdly inert.
reviews.author: Peter Tabakis

reviews.text: It's not the superhero stuff that worked for me. It's not the cameos, special effects, and Easter eggs. It's the heartfelt comedy and emotion that really works well.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: The Flash is good, but it lacks a stronger villain to antagonize and match up against Barry Allen, especially in the Scarlet Speedster's first big-screen outing.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: While I can’t quite recommend The Flash, I’m likewise certain there are plenty of potential viewers out there who will have a grand time watching Barry sprint from one corner of the multiverse to the other, and that’s just fine.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: "The Flash" delivers the spectacle and interactions fans have craved as well as more heart than expected.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: This super crowd-pleaser offers fun on infinite earths! The collision of tones works, triggering laughter and tears at times, thanks to a great direction and central performance. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: The Flash simply never becomes the film it could have so easily been.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: A movie that surprisingly balances the outsized action thrills with emotional heft.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: While The Flash as a movie is a bit of an overconfident, underdelivering mess, it is never truly boring.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: The Flash is essentially an ugly movie with some ugly special effects that shine a lot. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: It quickly turns into such a blur of nonsense that its early charms are all but wiped away, and the film runs out of steam as it drags to the nearly two-and-a-half hour mark.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The Flash is guaranteed entertainment from start to finish. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Antonio G. Spíndola

reviews.text: An utterly bizarre mishmash of whatever prevailing corporate ideology was batting Muschietti and company about the stormy seas of production.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: I never expected to be so emotionally invested in a summer superhero movie about a character I care so little about, but this is one of the better films in the DCEU canon.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: It feels like a movie that should have been released as the conclusion of a long and well-made phase, and not after the failure of a Universe that is about to be replaced by another. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: The Flash has its moments, but passes in the very opposite of a flash and, as so often with DC movies, the humour at times feels desperately forced, some of it unworthy of the most mediocre sitcom.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Above all, The Flash is a movie about the time we know we'll never get back. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Fernandez

reviews.text: Michael Keaton isn't the only one of Gotham's caped Crusaders to reappear, and his relaxed presence provides some of the movie's best moments. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Marcelo Stiletano

reviews.text: The long troubled production is without question a flashy *ahem* good time, but isn't quite worth the wait due to some shockingly sub-par CG visuals and a lack of depth for every supporting character aside from The Flash himself.
reviews.author: Kyle Wilson

reviews.text:
At times the movie is a bit too goofy for its own good. Muschetti’s use of pop songs during moments of epic action and crisis undermine the movie’s emotional investment. 
On the whole, we still recommend The Flash as an entertaining romp.
reviews.author: David Reddish

reviews.text: Though not groundbreaking, The Flash is fun. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: The Flash does pass the time. But then it begins to rewind it -- too often -- and in the end, feels pointless.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: The Flash is not the best superhero movie by a wide margin... Heck, it’s not even the best DCEU movie... But is it one of the best DCEU movies? You bet. ... [And] the right and best choice is to recast the role.
reviews.author: Mark Hughes

reviews.text: Muschietti adopts an exuberantly maximalist approach that’s stronger on energy than finesse.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: A basically entertaining, but flimsy and shallow object, The Flash may not be the final entry in this long-beleaguered franchise, but it might as well be.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: Lighter-than-air storytelling, coupled with great performances by Miller and Calle, with an especially powerful contribution by Keaton, make The Flash the year’s best superhero movie to date.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Director Andy Muschietti and his crew have crafted a superhero film for the ages with The Flash.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: It’s easily the weakest of the recent movies about multiple universes.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: When the inevitable multiverse cameos arrive – even those canonical embarrassments now reclaimed as easter eggs for fans – it's difficult to engage beyond a level of fleeting, nostalgic amusement.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: Amid the din, the same thing that left the film near-unreleasable is what makes it halfway watchable: Miller.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: In the end, the emotion of The Flash wins the day and certainly people who have more nostalgia for the Keaton Batman films will probably enjoy it more than I did
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: A mammoth misfire...The Speed Force is clearly not with The Flash. It sputters along down a road that leads nowhere.
reviews.author: Saibal Chatterjee

reviews.text: I wasn't expecting The Flash to save the entire DC Extended Universe, but I had hopes that it would send the old guard out on a high note. Instead it simply limps towards an unforeseen future.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: [T]he movie ultimately feels as if it's circling around a limited portrayal of the potential of this time-traveling/multiverse plot.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Miller...is easily the best thing about [the] movie, which starts out strong but...degenerates into rote CGI action in the second half, in the process also capitulating to the nostalgia bug and multiverse mania that have been infecting the genre of late.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: The Flash strives to appease apparent studio demands, the fickle love of fans, the gnawing yearning for nostalgia, and the increasingly impossible task of finding something new to say while repeating the same stories, and succeeds at none of it.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: The Flash has finally arrived and should wow audiences thanks to its dazzling special effects and Michael Keaton’s return as Batman.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: The Flash bets on nostalgia and forgets about the future, for better or worse.
reviews.author: Orlando Maldonado

reviews.text: The Flash finds a balance between fan service and a story for general audiences. The resulting movie gets dark without surrendering to the ennui that has cast its shade over so many of the other DC movies.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: 'The Flash' is the most entertaining an IP reset has ever been.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: While I also don't love 'that part everyone is mad at,' the big NON-CGI punchline they've chosen to end on is such a glorious 'Go F yourselves!' to the last three decades of toxic internet comic book movie fandom in I can't NOT respect the hell out of it.
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: The fan-service cameos that dominate the third act are mostly just ugly digital blips, and the action climax is repetitive and underwhelming.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Like its main hero, The Flash doesn't hide how hungry it is to be seen as worthy, even though it spends much of its time running on empty.
reviews.author: Glen Weldon

reviews.text: …how well the reprise of Keaton’s Batman initially works only underlines that the central core of The Flash is posted missing…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: But “The Flash” film wisely capitalizes on personalities, thus the intrigue builds in smart cameos, bounteous Easter eggs, and captivating performances both sentimental and sassy.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Definitely clocks in as a top-tier superhero adventure, it's overriding quality being how, unlike so many other $200 million superhero epics, you can actually remember it five minutes after hitting the exit.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: The film is the antithesis of every cinematically daring idea we've seen explored in multiversal storytelling in recent years. The fact that two of the best examples of this are so fresh in our memory only makes it seem worse. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario Alegre

reviews.text: Despite an electrifying start, The Flash gets overlong and bloated that it becomes a chore to sit through, but Keaton’s Batman still makes it watchable.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: The Flash is the best DC movie since The Dark Knight Rises.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: … the never-ending humor, miracle casting, excellent action sequences, bright script, and spot-on direction offer its audience a wonderful undertaking at the multiplex.
reviews.author: Elias Savada

reviews.text: If The Flash is meant to bookend the DCEU of the past decade or so, it certainly delivers, thanks to Muschietti’s distinctive tone and execution.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: A satisfying superhero saga with a beating heart.
reviews.author: Suchin Mehrotra

reviews.text: A solidly entertaining if predictable time-travel film that boasts something most DC movies sorely lack: a strong lead performance.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: I liked “The Flash” well enough while watching it.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: It’s not perfect, and maybe a bit too long, but it looks and feels much more like a creative vision than a lot of recent superhero output.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: Long on fan service and littered with incredulous plot manipulations, “The Flash” will work for DCEU diehards but only mildly entertain everyone else.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The question for me was whether or not I could endure an entire film that starts out with The Flash popping a baby in a microwave oven and slamming the door on it. Director Andy Muschietti clearly dropped the baby, er, ball, on this one.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: ...[The Flash] is a notable step in the right direction as we prepare for a new era of DC movies.
reviews.author: Thomas Stoneham-Judge

reviews.text: While the CGI leaves much to be desired, the story delivered all the laughs, action, fan service, and emotion I was hoping for. I had a blast.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: I mostly forgot about Miller’s real-life travails as this latest multi-versal tale motored along for much of its lengthy runtime, only to stumble in the final act. The Flash (like oh so many other movies) would benefit from a 20-minute trim.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: One of the final DCEU films under the current regime, The Flash goes in many different directions, none of which work very well.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: “The Flash” gets credit for effort, because this superhero movie isn’t trying to be stupid and convoluted. It gets there by accident.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: The film is remarkably banal. It’s a deteriorating rest stop on the road to nowhere.
reviews.author: Angelica Jade Bastién

reviews.text: It is a movie that dumps the moody angst of its predecessors and aims for fun, colourful action and enjoyable characters.
reviews.author: Andrew Gaudion

reviews.text: While director Andy Muschietti’s time-travel crowd pleaser doesn’t blaze any new narrative trails, it does result in a fun superhero nostalgic dive, for the most part.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Some moments seem like remnants of a first draft, full of narrative inconsistencies and unjustifiable leaps of characters' logic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Benjamín Harguindey

reviews.text: For some viewers, it seems that we are moving on a different timeline of what constitutes a great movie because The Flash is sadly not one of them.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: The Flash isn't a bad film at all... [But] I can be cynical about the blatant fan-service driving it.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: This is spaghetti-brained moviemaking, more interested in goosing empty-calorie nostalgia than telling an original or thrilling story.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: 'The Flash' is a superhero defined by his speed, yet his starring vehicle lumbers along like a 200-car freight train straining to climb a steep grade.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: The quippy performances and the nostalgia bait of Keaton et al might raise a smile. But it’s diminishing returns here...
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: ... An energetic, wild and wacky quest full of eye-popping and often surreal CGI that climaxes in an action-packed let's smash-everything third act.
reviews.author: George Simpson

reviews.text: The Flash delivers the nostalgia and the fun that DC fans have been waiting so long to witness on the big screen again.
reviews.author: Connor Petrey

reviews.text: The story moves fast (sorry) and the action scenes are thrilling, but the big surprise here is how funny it often is. And while it's there, the angst isn't overdone - all of which makes this one of the more solidly satisfying DCU movies to date.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: The good news is that Miller is up to the task. They are a strong actor with still untapped potential. Miller rises to the occasion with aplomb. The Flash/Barry Allen in stereo is eminently watchable and carries the movie on his back.
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: Far from the greatest superhero movie ever made and not quite among the worst, The Flash is still another mediocre effort from the DCEU with appalling VFX and a messy story that the excellent Michael Keaton and Sasha Calle alone are unable to save.
reviews.author: Josh Wilding

reviews.text: The Flash is a whole lot of film packed into a running time that you’d think would be able to contain such a story—but you’d be wrong. I still had a legit blast with some of what’s here, and that’s got to count for something.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: The Flash, about accepting the present and letting go of the past, packs a universe-spanning crossover tale with an emotional intimacy. The bad news is that the film itself can’t outrun the allure of the past, succumbing to the same vices it chides.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: Merely another in a string of lackluster big screen blockbusters.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: 'The Flash' is good, and occasionally flirts with excellence, but anyone who goes in heading the game-changer that was promised may be left feeling a touch short-changed.
reviews.author: Scott Campbell

reviews.text: Despite the rewarding return of Keaton (among others) and the consistent humor, there’s a striking scarcity of originality.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: THE FLASH is such an incoherent and at times downright ugly disaster that it’s almost fun again. But unfortunately, only almost.
reviews.author: Jimmy Cage

reviews.text: A fun superhero movie putting the pedal to the metal with action, laughs & thrills; not afraid of some silliness, without losing its emotional focus. I laughed, teared-up, & certainly applauded more than once. Absolutely loved it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: In the end, The Flash triumphs through its ability to connect emotionally and deliver moments of genuine humour. These elements, coupled with impressive action, make it a worthwhile watch.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: … unlikely to change your life, but as a sorta final film before James Gunn tries to cobble DC’s cinematic output together, it’s an engaging enough send off and a lowkey good time at the movies.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: The film has a lot of surprises up its sleeve, but aside from Keaton’s turn, it’s at its best when focussing on Barry Allen’s journey.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: We finally have a big budget Flash movie with all the bells/whistles to boot. Fan service aside (I cheered), the movie works for the greats Back to the Future vibe it has, and Ezra leads the charge quite well.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: A movie that wears its love for the comics that inspired it on its crimson-streaked sleeve. Funny, action-packed and effectively touching, anyone familiar with the DC stable of heroes should run, not walk, to see it.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: An endearing story that also has moments of maniacal action and meta fan service.
reviews.author: Craig D. Lindsey

reviews.text: The new film has it moments, thanks mainly to Miller, who brings a mesmerizing energy to dual roles.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: If only the whole film... felt this breezily clever and entertaining. Alas, the final act bogs down in what feels like an endless, generic CGI battle and a kitchen-sink resolution that leaves one feeling just a little exhausted and somewhat confused.
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: A well-acted but overlong adventure.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Keaton is the one who brings both effortless gravity and subtle levity to a film that, without him, wouldn't have much of either.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: You'll laugh, often, but Ezra Miller's solo saga squanders too much potential.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: It works in short bursts, and there’s an interesting – albeit at this point, unoriginal – idea in there, but on the whole The Flash is a messy, chaotic, and pandering attempt to salvage something out of a franchise that is/was going nowhere fast.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: One of the greatest superhero movies ever made? The Flash isn't even the best superhero movie released this month, but that doesn't mean it's not worth your time.
reviews.author: Mark Cassidy

reviews.text: While fun, this attempt to build meaning around the latest superhero story to tackle loss and what comes with great power (hint: it’s responsibility) makes the overarching narrative feel a bit middling, no matter how many gimmicks this movie has to offer.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Is The Flash an incoherent, overly meta, IP show & tell mess, or is it one of the most inventive and crowd-pleasing films in years? If the multiverse has taught us anything, it’s that multiple things can be true at the same time.
reviews.author: Joey Morona

reviews.text: The weakness of this movie is balanced out by the greatness. There are some wonderful moments in the "The Flash" including the return of Michael Keaton as Batman.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: ...it’s so cluttered with quick cuts of CG animation and constant loud blasts of crashing sounds, it’s hard to digest what you’re looking at. Go for the fun cameos, but for a film all about speed, this time line feels like forever.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Turns out it's worth the wait.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: The action is hit or miss, and the humor lands in a lot of scenes.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: It’s nuts. It’s fun.
reviews.author: Soren Andersen

reviews.text: Every bit as fun as it looks. This is comic book adaptation and fan service at a high level.
reviews.author: Paul Salfen

reviews.text: A jumbled culmination of Hollywood’s obsession with IP and nostalgia masquerading as an earnest time-skipping adventure.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: A jubilantly overcrowded, hyper-bloated superhero sci-fi carnival ride with a flip, fun, wildly inventive spin of comicdom's nostalgia wheel and a boatload of superstar cameos, overlapping timelines and a bombastic blowout of boom-boom-y CGI spectacle.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: It's a barrage on the senses matched with a steady-flow of the only currency Hollywood seems to deal in these days: Fan-service.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: I wonder how well Hollywood would survive financially without comic book films from the likes  of DC and Marvel.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: There is much to love in The Flash but it’s also one of the most egregious cases of fan service.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: The Flash manages to piece together just enough fun moments, superficial fan service, and emotional scenes to limp past the cinematic finish line.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: With universes colliding and diverging, the movie dials the evocative elements way up by way of surprising cameos, all the way to the ending. Rapidly kinetic action sequences, hilarious hijinks, inventive storytelling and heartwarming nostalgia.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: The Flash is undeniably entertaining. Full of humor, great action sequences, good dose of nostalgia and with a sweet (emotional) story at its core. It's messy, but still very fun. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: We’re all feeling a bit multi-versed out right now in the wake of Spider-Man: Across The Spider-Verse. But The Flash still speeds along nicely – no mean feat when it’s 2 hours 25min long.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: The Flash is a superhero film that prioritizes silliness with a cheese factor of gargantuan proportions, but no actual entertainment values whatsoever. It's special effects heavy and yet most shots involving an adequate amount of CGI are abysmal.
reviews.author: Chris Sawin

reviews.text: The entertainment factor is high.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Average writing, below average effects, and a refusal to embrace its emotional core make for a mediocre viewing experience far longer than The Flash provides anything great.
reviews.author: Michael Walsh

reviews.text: This is a Flash movie -- how is the speed? The speed's absolutely satisfying. It feels fast and it hits hard. There are some effects they do in this movie that enhance the feeling of speed and punch that I didn't see in the Justice League.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: What ought to have been a proper send-off to the DCEU as we've come to know it and should have just been a standalone Flash tale instead is a misbegotten grab bag of "remember when"s.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: It’s nice to be reminded that live action superhero movies can be well written too.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: A dire end to a dire franchise, "The Flash" is a waste of time grounded by a poor lead, disastrous special effects, and a depressing marquee cameo.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: The nostalgia factor will leave fans satisfied. The over reliance on, not always perfect special effects, will leave most a bit winded
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: The last remnants of the near-defunct DCU once again reveal a desperation to catch-up to what has come before and relying on a nostalgia museum instead of earning the big wow and emotional beats it so craves.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: It remains an entertaining sit and a real adrenaline shot for the DCEU, but after 90 minutes of zooming, bantering, and mourning, “The Flash” runs out of dramatic material.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: 144 minutes is way over the top for what we get.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Muschietti’s efforts seem only to function as a conduit for the many cameos stuffed into this movie.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: The Flash is the good DC movie.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: The Flash gets a lot right. The writing for both versions of Barry is excellent, and the emotional scenes work extremely well. The cgi is rough in spots, but certain stylized moments are great.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: The story gets messy — multiple cameos and a rushed intro for Sasha Calle as Supergirl — but I like how it follows Keaton’s war cry: “Let’s get nuts.”
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: The Flash delivers a fun & crowd-pleasing adventure across time and the DC universe. A nice variety of action and plot points keeps your interest while a bit too much humor and some shockingly distracting CG effects keep this from being a knockout win.
reviews.author: Cody Leach

reviews.text: It has its drawbacks and doesn't quite shine, but it delivers good entertainment... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: For all its flaws, The Flash proves strong on character where it counts as it serves up its MCU-style comedy, tragedy, and wow-factor visuals...In the final equation, the Scarlet Speedster gives us a largely enjoyable run for our summer-movie money.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: If it's not even close to being the best superhero movie of June 2023, let alone of all time, The Flash delivers enough blockbuster thrills and surprising fan service to satisfy DC fans.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: While 'The Flash' does boast unusual narrative complexity and character depth, it does succumb at times to ensemble overload.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Action packed from beginning to end, “The Flash” is the DC movie fans have been waiting for.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: The story packs in surprises while also telling a very cohesive, understandable, and hilarious multiverse movie. A lot of the CGI leaves a bunch to be desired, but the performances and character journey are what make this an enjoyable and memorable watch.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: A screwball sophomoric comedy that feels more like Whedon's brief venture into the DCEU than a connected piece to what Snyder built. Great performance(s) by Ezra, but relies too much on nostalgic moments that are more worthy of eye rolls than cheers.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: Visually stunning and exhilarating despite an uneven tone. It's one of the most wildly entertaining, surprising and funny superhero movies since Deadpool.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Even in a vacuum, or an alternate universe with no Spider-Verse or MCU, The Flash would just feel middling.
reviews.author: Liz Shannon Miller

reviews.text: Peppered with fanservice cameos, this amusing DC franchise crossover arrives several years too late to make an impact.
reviews.author: Gavia Baker-Whitelaw

reviews.text: The Flash might feature some of these good moments, but they don't add up to anything, and at the end of the day, the film as a whole is an overly long mess with a few bright spots and a massive missed opportunity when it comes to Supergirl.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: You know the movie has some issues when the audience is more excited to see the supporting cast and cameo appearances as opposed to watching the lead.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: The film’s parade of “remember this?!” in-jokes makes it the opposite of a reset – it’s more like a scratched record.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Muschietti proves he can coherently direct different set pieces and make Ezra Miller's physical humor work quite efficiently. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: The Flash is everything that much of the last 10 years of DC-based movies have not been: It's fast-paced, character-driven, and, most importantly, in love with the comics and the iconic superheroes themselves.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: Although it’s not without some fun moments, The Flash often substitutes cameos for genuine thrills, and a general aura of exhaustion hovers over it all.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: Runs around in circles.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Not only do we get a great love letter to all things DC, but we also showcase one of the better Flash stories told.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Set to be one of the final entries in what we know as the DCEU, this is also one of the best, a witty and warm buddy comedy that deserves to be more than just a Flash in the pan.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt (UK)

reviews.text: The movie puts a lot of thought into what it wants to say and not enough into how it says it.
reviews.author: Matt Zoller Seitz

reviews.text: I'm suffering from a little bit of multiverse fatigue. But highlights include Supergirl and Michael Keaton as Batman.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: It’s strange to be watching and reviewing another superhero movie, like 'The Flash,' in the wake of 'Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse,' which, by comparison, is like measuring gourmet with fast food. That said, 'The Flash' is some tasty fast food.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: A reasonably entertaining, multiverse-themed superhero adventure.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: The best chemistry in the whole film is the one that Ezra Miller has with Ezra Miller. (...) Flash is more an homage to what the DC universe was rather than a reset button. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jesus Agudo

reviews.text: White noise fan service that doesn’t register as anything beyond pointless action devoid of character-driven stakes, filled with horrendous CGI. Ezra Miller is the only decent aspect, and I shudder to think how awful The Flash would be without them
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Feels like the first DC film in a long time — like Superman II long -- that finds the ideal balance of action, engaging plot, likable characters whose default personality isn’t shades of brooding with equal parts pathos and fun.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: A little flashy for a summer blockbuster film. But overall The Flash is quirky, quick witted, emotional and relatable with his own twist on the DC multiverse. Just a little too super hyped.
reviews.author: Christie Cronan

reviews.text: Ezra Miller is definitely an acquired taste as the lead character...Perhaps most troubling of all is how much more interesting both the older Batman character (Michael Keaton) and the new Supergirl character (Sasha Calle) are in support.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Falling victim of its own thematic mantra, The Flash refuses to let go of the past, instead allowing it to define what it has become in the present – in other words, a hodgepodge of former glories, with no clear identity of its own.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: The Flash is a fun and adventurous film that brings a lot of nostalgia and DC goodness into the fold. And Michael Keaton as Batman is definitely the highlight of the film.
reviews.author: John Nguyen

reviews.text: The Flash is a satisfying superhero experience, complete with epic scale, heartfelt emotion, a back door origin story, and a few issues along the way.
reviews.author: Germain Lussier

reviews.text: What The Flash bungles in franchise reconstruction and formal execution, it gets right in fan service and momentary pleasures.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: This first feature film featuring the subatomically fast DC Comics hero is a zippy and entertaining blast. And yet it nonetheless manages to serve up a few heartfelt moments amid all its carefully choreographed chaos.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: For as much as all the talk of portending fate leads to dashing heroics in the extravagant The Flash, one can slow their roll, step back, and see plenty of the hot mess and crapshoot Michael Keaton's Batman was talking about in character.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Ezra Miller saves the Snyderverse in a stunning superhero adaptation that gloriously lives up to the hype. The Flash is the DC film that fans have been aching to see.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: The Flash was a dazzling visual extravaganza that will get you pumped for the multiverse. The emotional weight is heavy, backed by two wonderful Batman. You sympathize with Barry Allen, and this is one of the better comic book films in recent years.
reviews.author: Brandon Avery

reviews.text: As another comic book offering hoping to leap around any fatigue audiences may be experiencing from a relative over-saturation, its Back To The Future-inspired mentality places it on a higher plane than many of its fellow DCEU counterparts.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: While the core conceit of Warner Bros. Discovery’s The Flash is solid, the movie’s too-meta nostalgia plays highlight everything that has gone awry with the studio’s superhero movie experiment.
reviews.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore

reviews.text: Director Andy Muschietti delivers an emotional film filled with nostalgia and throwbacks to previous films. It's the most satisfying film to date from the DCEU in the past decade. The movie will do bonkers business with repeat viewings.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: ... all the sins and triumphs of DC's past cinematic aspirations have been laid bare in a grand parade... one the most watchable DC films in the last decade merely by standing on the shoulders of everything that's come before.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: ...The Flash resets the universe in spectacular fashion.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: More smiles per hour than expected and the cameos quickly become one of this film's highlights. Ezra Miller acquits himself well as the troubled young man who goes back in time to save his mother and meets a carefree version of himself.
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: Considering how “The Flash” makes many of its characters face death and inevitability throughout, “The Flash” should not feel as hollow as it does.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: Predictably disjointed and messy coming out of such a problematic production, but it’s not enough to slow down a genuine love for the character.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: ...if not for all the baggage, there’s a real chance Miller’s performances here could have been in the awards conversation.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: Bold, creative, and with some appealing quirks, The Flash lives up to expectations and offers some jaw-dropping surprises. Viewers who are new to the DC Extended Universe (DCEU) won’t get too confused, while ardent fans will be constantly thrilled.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: It culminates in a chaotic third-act climax... in the kind of glossy and distracting charade that hopes you’ll be so gobsmacked by the sheer sight of revived crime-fighters from yesteryear that you’ll neglect to ask: why?
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: To offer the film any kind of praise is an uneasy task, because its star is one of the most controversial Hollywood figures in recent memory.
reviews.author: Allegra Frank

reviews.text: It’s a pitiful disservice to itself, turning a relatively fun, if rocky, movie into nothing but another product designed as a carousel where you can point at things and people you recognize.
reviews.author: Trace Sauveur

reviews.text: Despite a promising start, The Flash is not the multiverse game-changer it wants to be seen as - it barely feels like a final draft.
reviews.author: Rory Doherty

reviews.text: The Flash is one of its strongest entries and should, even with some flaws, be considered a jewel in the DCU crown.
reviews.author: Simon Thompson

reviews.text: At the end of the day, it’s a fine movie, which is good for DC as a whole. DC’s live-action offerings just already include a brilliant Flash story from Grant Gustin’s Barry, and so the movie simply pales in comparison.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: The Flash feels caught between too many things it wants to keep ahold of (which flies against the film’s lesson of letting go). It feels like a brand that wants to have all its cards on the table in case it wants to pivot to the most popular one.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: What makes Andy Muschietti’s The Flash a great movie is it’s not about saving the universe.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: Taken on its own merits, Andy Muschietti’s film has lots to offer, and frequently shows flashes (apologies) of brilliance that set it a cut above most of its existing DC Universe brethren.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: Is it fun? Yes, absolutely. Is it good? I don’t really know.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: It's well-trod territory at this point, even for a speedster.
reviews.author: Christian Holub

reviews.text: It’s not terrible, but it’s not as great as the initial reactions claimed either, and it’s certainly not the best superhero movie in [insert number of years here].
reviews.author: Britany Murphy

reviews.text: The Flash is a visually spectacular superhero and sci-fi drama that works best when it keeps its characters at the forefront.
reviews.author: Swara Salih

reviews.text: A time-traveling, time-tripping fantasy, The Flash is funny, inventive and giddy -- like the Back to the Future franchise for superheroes.
reviews.author: Tom Gliatto

reviews.text: Maybe nerd culture was a mistake.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: It’s sometimes buried under layers and layers of storytelling knots that the film never fully untangles, but the fun is there, and when the film is really working, that turns out to be enough.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: This is one of the best superhero movies of the 21st century so far. Just sit back and enjoy the flashes of greatness.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Probably not the BEST superhero movie ever made, but it's certainly the funniest! Ezra Miller is a tour de force with a career best performance, while Keaton & Calle offer fantastic support. Reminiscent of classics like Batman 1989, Spider-Man 2002 & X2.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: The Flash is, by far, the best movie to come out of this modern, post-Nolan Warners/DC collaboration...
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: Despite some diverting touches, Miller’s smirking, gurning, mugging doppelganger performance is a trial and in any case gets lost in the inevitable third-act CGI battle apocalypse.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: The Flash, much like Barry himself, has been stranded with no real sense of history, and no real sense of the future, either. It does the best it can.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: I guess I’m supposed to be impressed. I’m not; I was bored as hell.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: The Flash is a passable multiverse superhero movie, but no amount of DC cameos can make audiences forget the awful off-screen actions of Ezra Miller.
reviews.author: Molly Freeman

reviews.text: It plays the correct notes and is ingeniously outlandish in the right ways (including a perfect drop of its one allotted f-bomb), but excels when leading with its heart.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: The Flash nearly drowns itself in excess and profuse fan service, but this colossally-scaled superhero adventure hits the right notes when it maximizes on rousing personal stakes and nimble humor.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: The superhero fan service is strong with this one – perhaps too strong at times – but it never fully overshadows Barry Allen’s genuinely tragic and heartfelt story of grief.
reviews.author: Joshua Yehl

reviews.text: The Flash may be one of the better DCEU films in recent history, but it is the epitome of “check your brains at the door and just try to enjoy the ride.”
reviews.author: Maggie Lovitt

reviews.text: A wild and clever take on “Flashpoint,” and a fine punctuation mark to the Snyderverse.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: asily the best in the genre since Spiderman: No Way Home, this fresh, invigorating, and hugely entertaining summer treat is as good as it gets when it comes to cinematic takes on superheroes.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: "The Flash" provides an enjoyable if wildly uneven deep dive into a nostalgia-laden romp; now if only DC could manage to connect audiences with their contemporary characters.
reviews.author: Bill Watters

reviews.text: Worth the hype, though trying to do so much also leads to a head-scratching kitchen-sink climax.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: This film is a love letter made by a DC fan for a DC fan. It is abundantly clear that Andrés Muschietti loves DC and wanted to make a film that celebrated the legacy of DC.
reviews.author: Scott Menzel

reviews.text: The Flash finally exists in an undoubtedly fun, but somewhat inconsequential way. The movie's liveliness is infectious, and there are some genuinely unbelievable moments on display, but that might not fully cement it as a legendary part of DC's canon.
reviews.author: Jenna Anderson

reviews.text: Cameos and fan service are fine to have, but the story has to be there to back them up, and it’s not quite there with The Flash.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: The Flash is a bright, colorful, imaginative film with enough verve to pop off the screen, even though it’s often nonsensical in its wibbly-wobbly, timey-wimey stuff.
reviews.author: Joshua Rivera

reviews.text: Perhaps it’s no surprise that Barry Allen’s fitfully fun, fan-service-freighted headline act sometimes looks like an expanded universe imploding to ambitious but often messy effect.
reviews.author: Kevin Harley

reviews.text: In The Flash, the multiverse of possibilities that opens up by toying with the past becomes an excuse to throw everything but the Batcave sink at the audience.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: While director Andy Muschietti lets bad FX, in-joke cameos and muddled time-travel mechanics sprawl out on the couch and stay awhile longer, within its template the movie does have a peculiar, likable energy.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: A movie that spends all its time racing from one poorly-thought out story element to another, from one only modestly satisfying nostalgia shout-out to another, and with only questionable results. How fitting, yet how disappointing: The Flash has the runs.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: The Flash is a funny, emotional, action-heavy crowd-pleaser.
reviews.author: Ben Pearson

reviews.text: The Flash is the big DC adventure you've been waiting for.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: If The Flash ultimately proves uneven, its wobbly climactic showdown far less interesting than the more character-driven buildup, the story’s core of a young man struggling to reconcile with the loss of his mother carries it through.
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: A better time-travel movie than a superhero movie. The film has playful fun exploring permutations in time, and contains genuine emotion, if not overwrought thrills.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: As fun as the movie is, what elevates The Flash is a genuinely weighty concept explored with all the bombast fans expect from the franchise.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: Seeing Keaton’s Batman was fun alongside all the other surprise cameos but one can’t help but feel like it’s more empty spectacle than substance.
reviews.author: Catherine Gonzales

reviews.text: It’s not quite the disaster that some of the previous DC films have been yet it never fully finds its own identity.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: Ultimately, "The Flash" doesn't reinvent the superhero genre by any means, but it's still one of the most consistently entertaining entries in the genre in years.
reviews.author: Daniel Howat

reviews.text: Michael Keaton’s Batman return saves this movie.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: A love letter to DC movies of the past and present, this movie is packed with action, humor, a ton of heart, and lots of fan service. The CGI is wonky and Supergirl is underused, but it is an absolute joy to see Keaton back as Batman.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Nothing Batman or Supergirl do in The Flash to save the world is more effective than what Barry Allen does to save it with a hug and a can of tomatoes.
reviews.author: Justin Clark

reviews.text:
The Flash is solid. Ezra Miller and Sasha Calle shine brightest in the film, but the film is encumbered with poor vision.

Plot threads and writing is befuddling, and VFX leaves a lot to be desired. Overall, The Flash is entertaining but a very mixed bag.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: What if Back to the Future Part II met the DC Universe? Director Andy Muschietti’s The Flash answers that question with a nostalgic journey filled with stunning action, emotional stakes, heart, humor, and universe-bending time travel.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

synopsis: Worlds collide in "The Flash" when Barry uses his superpowers to travel back in time in order to change the events of the past. But when his attempt to save his family inadvertently alters the future, Barry becomes trapped in a reality in which General Zod has returned, threatening annihilation, and there are no Super Heroes to turn to. That is, unless Barry can coax a very different Batman out of retirement and rescue an imprisoned Kryptonian... albeit not the one he's looking for. Ultimately, to save the world that he is in and return to the future that he knows, Barry's only hope is to race for his life. But will making the ultimate sacrifice be enough to reset the universe?
